Anchor.Suffix: whose text files are indexed on

Applied.Outcome: Corpus items are uploaded zips, indexed on upload; they replace filespecs, so the server never reads outside ~data.

Replies.Text:
"The corpus" needs a definition. I suggest one **root folder per project** (for example a repository path in the project's settings), with filespecs as globs relative to it. Reading outside `~data` is new for this server, so the root should come only from the owner's settings, never from a request.

These files change outside Consensus, and our index is only refreshed on changes Consensus makes. Filespec items need a check by modification time at search or Send time, plus a size limit and a text-only filter so binary files are skipped.

A project may have multiple "corpus" items.
This kind of item should be a zip file whose contents constitute the corpus.

**Outcome:** a project can have any number of **Corpus** items. Each one is a zip file uploaded into the project and stored in its folder. Its text files are indexed on upload, binary and oversized files are skipped, and uploading a new zip over it re-indexes it.

This replaces filespecs, so the server never reads outside `~data`, and the re-index check by modification time isn't needed.

Applied.Outcome: One call per Send with project-scoped context from our own index; LLM tools are a later step.

Replies.Text:
Today the LLM has no tools. It gets one prompt and returns one JSON answer. "Direct query" implies either:

- **(a)** keep one call per Send, with search limited to the project and the prompt holding the best passages from project items and corpus files, or
- **(b)** a read/search tool loop, which changes `Llm.js` for both `claude-cli` and `ollama`.

I suggest (a) first. And does "vector search" mean our BM25 index, with Ollama vectors added when configured, or does it make Ollama required?

We do want to add tool usage and it can be done in a subsequent step.
This is using our custom vector embedding and search.

**Outcome:** this version keeps one LLM call per Send. Its context comes from our own index (BM25, with Ollama vectors added when configured), limited to the project and covering documents, plans and corpus files. Giving the LLM tools is a later step, in its own proposal.

Two questions on the shape:

**Outcome:**

- Every item belongs to exactly one project. To reuse an item elsewhere, copy it, then move the copy to the other project.

Since items never span projects, copy is now part of the design rather than something extra. What a copy carries is still open in the Copy-Paste thread.
